However, the veggie wings, cactus, and sweet potato burritos were delicious. The guacamole was also tasty, although the spicy chips were a bit overwhelming. input: I recently tried out this Thai restaurant and I would give it 4-5 stars. It was my first visit and I found the food to be delicious. The pad thai and drunken noodle dishes were also enjoyable, although the noodles in the pad thai were a bit overdone. The portions were slightly smaller than other places in the area. The owner was friendly and attentive, even coming outside to talk with me about the food. The restaurant has a cute setup in a quaint house, but it may not be ideal if it's crowded. I heard about this place from a fellow Yelp Elite and decided to give it a try with my SO. We went on a Saturday morning and had to wait in line. 

The takoyaki appetizer was delicious - perfectly cooked and topped with sauces. The fried octopus was good but didn't come with enough mayo. 

Unfortunately, the ramen noodles were overcooked and didn't fit well with the dishes. The broth was flavorful, but the red chili one was too spicy and covered up the depth. I preferred the black garlic broth. 

Overall, the food was tasty and reasonably priced. The decor was nice, but there were screaming kids running around which made our meal unpleasant.

input: I recently enjoyed an express lunch at this charming restaurant with old school decor featuring dark woods and a copper tile ceiling. The entree, garganelli with roast pork ragu, mushrooms, and creole tomatoes, was a delightful blend of flavors with a light sauce that highlighted the dish. The roast pork itself was tender, caramelized, and left me craving more. Overall, a satisfying lunch experience in a visually appealing setting.

input: I was highly impressed by the French-German dishes at Luke Restaurant in New Orleans. The historic vibe of the former Masonic Temple Building added to the overall experience. input: This is a typical Broad Ripple charming spot with a small, trendy, and bustling atmosphere. Unfortunately, they do not take reservations, which can be annoying for those traveling from another part of town. However, the cocktails were creative and delicious, and the server's suggestions were on point. The guacamole was tasty, but came with nuts despite requesting them to be left off. The Harvest salad was a highlight with its delightful combination of fruit and root vegetables. The Veracruz Trigger fish and Serrano Scallops were both delicious, accompanied by interesting white sweet mashed potatoes. The Tostones were a bit dry, but dipped in the Stewed Black Beans, they tasted great. Unfortunately, there were no gluten-free, dairy-free dessert options available. Overall, it's worth a visit, just make sure to arrive before 7 pm on a Friday to secure a table.

input: I've been to Jackson's multiple times and finally decided to leave a review. The panini Reuben was delicious with great use of garlic and perfectly sliced meat. However, the salad came out at the same time as the sandwich, which was not ideal, and the presentation was a bit sloppy. The sandwich was served directly on a plate instead of a napkin, causing the bread to get soggy if it sits for too long. The price is a bit high, but the food and drink quality justifies it. They have a great selection of wines and beers to choose from. The wait staff is generally friendly but can sometimes be short or distracted. The wait time for drinks can vary, with my longest wait being 15 minutes during a lunch rush. Overall, it was a good experience and I will return.

input: My girlfriends and I dined at the Creole House for dinner due to its proximity to our hotel. The bacon garlic oysters were average, as the flavors were overpowered by the cheese and bacon. The jumbo buffalo wings were tasty and well-seasoned. The jumbalaya pasta lacked flavor and was our least favorite, while the blackened red fish was just okay. The sautéed veggies accompanying the dish were excessively salty. The canal street red fish wasn't great and lacked garlic sauce. The paddle boat drinks tasted good but were more juice than alcohol. Overall, the food was underwhelming, earning the restaurant a solid 3 stars. On a positive note, our server, Alexander, provided excellent hospitality and tried his best to ensure our satisfaction.

input: This is hands down my favorite sushi spot in Delaware. The menu is simple yet executed perfectly, with reasonably priced rolls that are bursting with fish. The use of flash-frozen sashimi grade fish doesn't compromise the flavor, as the color, texture, taste, and smell are all flawless. The spicy tuna roll is nothing short of incredible, thanks to the combination of kewpie mayo, sriracha, and sichimi powder. I can't get enough of this place, often having it for lunch every day for weeks. The addition of short-grain brown sushi rice has been a fantastic touch. Watching YC Park, The Sushiman, work his magic is mesmerizing, as he effortlessly skins a cucumber with a sushi knife and transforms it into a nori sheet for his rolls. The temaki rolls are massive, packed with fish, and the nigiri is beautifully presented. While I save my 5-star rating for places that serve locally caught fresh fish, Tokyo is a must-visit for sushi lovers. Support the owners in these challenging times and skip Kooma and save Mikimotos for a special night out. If you crave sushi, look no further than Tokyo!
